text:
Ashley: quick check — i'm about to merge a terraform change that updates the IRSA annotation for the telemetry-uploader serviceaccount to point at the rotated iam role. planning: canary in staging, then prod. does this require pod restarts? any gotchas with projected tokens or helm values?

Ben: you shouldn't need a full restart if the cluster uses projected serviceAccount tokens (TokenRequest API). new tokens will be minted for new token requests, but long-lived in-memory creds in the app won't refresh automatically. if the app caches creds, you might need a restart or a graceful token refresh.

Shiv: can you paste the terraform and sa yaml snippets? want to double-check the annotation key and that we're not accidentally changing automount flags. also, which cluster version is staging? older clusters had different behavior.

Ashley: sure — snippets below. staging is on EKS 1.25, prod 1.26.

Ashley: ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: telemetry-uploader
  namespace: telemetry
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/telemetry-uploader-rotated
automountServiceAccountToken: true
```

Ashley: terraform (module snippet):
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_service_account" "telemetry" {
  metadata {
    name = "telemetry-uploader"
    namespace = "telemetry"
    annotations = {
      "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = aws_iam_role.telemetry.arn
    }
  }
}

resource "aws_iam_role" "telemetry" {
  name = "telemetry-uploader-rotated"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.eks_assume_role.json
}
```

infra-bot: terraform plan: 1 to change, 0 to add, 0 to destroy (serviceaccount.metadata.annotations[eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn])

Kevin: heads-up — if you toggle the annotation, EKS will accept it immediately but existing pods that already have tokens might keep using old ones until they request a new token. for most apps that call sts:AssumeRole every request, no change. for apps that reuse tokens, plan a quick pod restart cadence.

Ben: for minimal blast radius: do canary in telemetry namespace: deploy rotated role to a canary deployment (telemetry-uploader-canary), verify it can write to S3, check CloudTrail for AssumeRole calls. then roll the annotation in staging, wait 15–30m, then prod. add a fallback role with broader permissions only if needed.

Shiv: small suggestion: in terraform we should set `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations] }`? be careful — that suppresses drift detection. maybe better: do an explicit resource patch with `kubectl patch` in the rollout step so tf state stays stable.

Ashley: good point — i don't want to ignore annotation changes in tf. plan is: 1) create new iam role + policy (tf) 2) create canary deployment referencing new sa (k8s) 3) smoke test 4) apply annotation change (tf apply) 5) if apps need restarts, do `kubectl rollout restart` on deployment(s) in small batches 

Kevin: +1. also add a short TTL on projected tokens if you can (serviceAccountTokenProjection) so rotation surface is smaller. e.g., in pod spec: `serviceAccountToken: { audiences: ["sts.amazonaws.com"], expirationSeconds: 900 }` depending on lib support.

Ben: one more nit: watch IAM role session names in CloudTrail for the canary to ensure it's using the right role. set up a short alert if assume-role fails with 403.

Ashley: who can review the tf PR? @Ben @Shiv? i'd like to merge tomorrow morning and do canary in staging after lunch.

Ben: can do a quick pass this afternoon. i'll focus on the iam policy boundaries and trust relationship.

Shiv: i'll review the k8s manifests and helm values; i'll also check the cluster flags for projected token support.

Ashley: thanks — i'll add a small runbook in the PR with rollback steps: how to revert annotation (tf) and how to restart pods if needed.

Kevin: sounds good. ping me when canary passes; i'll coordinate prod window. :thumbsup:

Ashley: updated plan added to the PR and short runbook included. tagging reviewers.```
